labels.label: theo:universality_tori
labels.notes: Unmarked in the module docstring (`theo:universality_tori` — main.tex:291) and status partial: correct. The declaration statements are unchanged since aeae8df (comment-stripped comparison), so AUDIT-1's and AUDIT-2's faithfulness checks still stand. Corrected forms: universality_tori_of_ergodic, universality_tori, universality_tori_iff, isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff. Printed form: UniversalityToriPrinted over AffineToroidalModel with IsPrintedToriCondition = l.820, refuted by not_universalityToriPrinted given hex. The constant-heads refutations are unconditional for d >= 1. The new disclosures are true. (a) GL_d(Z) in UniversalityToriPrinted is called a strengthening of a refuted Prop, in checklist row 1, its docstring (l.1148-1150), REPORT hypotheses row 1 and finding 1. Calling it immaterial is right: moves meeting l.820 exist in SL_d(Z) for d >= 2, e.g. generators of SL_d(Z) with their inverses and b = 0, since SL_d(Z) leaves no proper rational subspace invariant and is not amenable. That is not in Lean, and the text says so. (b) Translations are a function of the parameter (AffineToroidalModel docstring l.864-869, SCOPE l.75-78, question 2, C-31 note). With all of them free, l.820 fails at some parameter for d >= 1: for j != i the inverse relation b_j = -A_i^{-1} b_i, and for j = i the relation (I + A_i) b_i = 0, each define a proper closed subgroup of (T^d)^p (the second unless A_i = -I). A finite union of proper closed subgroups has Haar measure 0. If every A_i = -I, the linear parts {+-I} satisfy (ii) with W = 0. So in that reading the printed theorem is vacuous, as disclosed. At d = 0 the claim fails (minor 3). (c) Continuity is not encoded, the refuting models are continuous, and a one-point model also refutes: all three are disclosed. 'No satisfiable assumption on the Phi_i alone' and 'T-egf-tori-minimal (planned)' are fixed in the docstring (l.1126-1127), SCOPE (l.84), finding 1, finding 4, the C-28 note and kb_proposals. The roadmap has T-egf-tori-minimal as planned.

checked_findings.finding: REPORT labels[0].findings[2] and corrections[0] (C-28) notes, the rewritten aperiodicity passage
checked_findings.verdict: true, presented as unformalized; two wording points (minors 1 and 2)
checked_findings.notes: 'Bekka-Guivarc'h's criterion for a spectral radius < 1 ... assumes the generating measure aperiodic' matches bg.txt l.57-60 ('Assume that mu is aperiodic ... Then the action ... has a spectral gap if and only if r(U0(mu)) < 1'). The minimal four moves S^{+-1}, T^{+-1} are periodic, because S -> -1, T -> -1 is a homomorphism SL_2(Z) -> {+-1} (C-28 (a)). The Kesten clause is right. L2_0(T^2) is, by Fourier, the permutation representation on Z^2 - 0. The stabilizer of a primitive vector is conjugate to the unipotent group, isomorphic to Z and amenable. So the representation is weakly contained in the regular representation, the norm of the symmetric average is at most Kesten's rho < 1 (SL_2(Z) is not amenable), and the spectrum lies in [-rho, rho]. The general sketch is right, re-derived independently. Since ||P|| <= 1, a spectral value z with |z| = 1 lies on the boundary of the spectrum, hence in the approximate point spectrum. Uniform convexity then gives U(Phi_i) xi_n - z xi_n -> 0 for each move. c_h := lim <U(h) xi_n, xi_n> is well defined and multiplicative: two words for h with exponent sums e and e' force z^{e - e'} = 1. K = ker c is normal, H/K is abelian, and U(k) xi_n - xi_n -> 0 on K, so K satisfies (ii) by Theorem 5 (K is countable). Then H satisfies (ii). Take W' = the intersection over h in H of p_a(h)W. It is a finite intersection by dimension and H-invariant, and W' is contained in W, which is not Q^d. Q^d/W' embeds K-equivariantly in a finite product of the Q^d/p_a(h_j)W, on each of which the image of p_a(K) is conjugate to its amenable image on Q^d/W. The image of H extends that amenable group by a quotient of H/K, which is abelian, so it is amenable. For the record: AUDIT-2's version says 'the finitely many distinct p_a(h)W', but H/K may be infinite and the orbit of W with it. Only the intersection is finite, which is all the argument needs. The REPORT does not carry that phrase. The REPORT's text ends 'Not formalized and not used', so the sketch is not presented as proved.

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].findings[2] ('So the paper's route l.818 -> l.273 -> Theorem 3.4 does not fail at its own example; ergodicity is all this file needs') and corrections[0] (C-28) notes (same sentence)
findings.what: The sentence is the negation of AUDIT-2's paraphrase and says more than the gap argument shows. The argument shows that the spectral-gap step works at the paper's example for d >= 2: l.818's gap holds two-sidedly, so l.273 applies in C-30's corrected two-sided form. It does not show that the route works. Theorem 3.4 still needs the family to contain the mixing policy together with dense outflows: C-31, and the REPORT's own finding 1 says the printed Theorem 3.5 is false for every choice of linear parts. And the paper's example is stated 'in any dimension' (l.293), but at d = 1 the route does fail (finding 4, C-28 (b)). Read on its own, the sentence tells the author that the paper's proof works at its example, which the same REPORT contradicts.
findings.fix: In both places write: 'So the spectral-gap step of the paper's route (l.818, then l.273 in C-30's two-sided form) holds at its own example for d >= 2; Theorem 3.4 still needs C-31's richness, and at d = 1 the route fails (C-28 (b)).'

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].findings[2] and corrections[0] (C-28) notes ('an eigenvalue of modulus 1 would give a character whose kernel has almost invariant vectors, hence satisfies (ii), hence so does the group')
findings.what: As written, the sketch excludes only eigenvalues of modulus 1. The two-sided gap (spectral radius < 1) needs every spectral value of modulus 1 excluded. Those are approximate eigenvalues, because P is a contraction and such a point lies on the boundary of its spectrum. That case is what the 'almost invariant vectors' in the sketch actually handle. Also, 'hence satisfies (ii)' leaves implicit that this step is Theorem 5 applied to the kernel, which is the cited Prop, not a proved fact. The wording is AUDIT-2's own and was adopted verbatim.
findings.fix: Write: 'a point of modulus 1 in the spectrum (an approximate eigenvalue, the operator being a contraction) would give a character whose kernel has almost invariant vectors, hence satisfies (ii) by Theorem 5, hence so does the group'.

There, 'free parameters' still describes AffineToroidalModel's translations, against the disclosed reading (a function of the parameter: free, tied or fixed) and against the refutation, which uses fixed translations. (b) The vacuity claim is true for d >= 1 only. At d = 0 every move is the identity, so inverse-stability holds. Not-(ii) also holds, since Q^0 has no proper subspace (as SCOPE l.82-83 itself says). So l.820 holds at every parameter, and the parenthetical 'unless every A_i = -I, whose linear parts satisfy (ii)' is false there (-I = I, and (ii) fails).
